blocks.content: Force and work are important concepts in physics that explain how objects move and interact. Force causes a change in the state of motion of an object, while work is done when a force causes displacement.
1. Meaning of Force

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Force is an external push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or uniform motion of a body.
Newton's First Law defines inertia, Second Law gives the formula F = ma, and Third Law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
Work is done when a force displaces an object in its direction, given by W = F × d × cos(θ).
Work can be positive, negative, or zero depending on the angle between the applied force and displacement.
Power represents the rate of doing work (P = W / t), with 1 Horsepower equal to 746 Watts.

blocks.content: • Force is a push or pull acting on an object.
• It can change the shape, direction or speed of an object.
• The SI unit of force is Newton (N).
• Force is a vector quantity.
2. Effects of Force
• Force can start or stop motion.
• It can change the speed of an object.
• It can change the direction of motion.
• It can change the shape or size of an object.
3. Types of Force
4. Newton’s Laws of Motion
Work is defined as the product of the magnitude of the force and the displacement in the direction of the force.
First Law (Law of Inertia):
An object remains at rest or continues in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
Second Law:
The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied force. Mathematically: F = ma
Third Law:
For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
5. Meaning of Work

rows: Energy transferred when a force causes displacement
The rate at which work is performed or energy is transferred

blocks.content: Work is said to be done when a force applied on an object causes displacement. The SI unit of work is Joule (J).
6. Formula of Work
Work = Force × Displacement
W = F × s
7. Types of Work
• Positive Work – When force and displacement are in the same direction.
• Negative Work – When force and displacement are in opposite directions.
• Zero Work – When displacement is zero.
8. Power
Power is the rate at which work is done.

items: 1 Horsepower (HP) is equal to 746 Watts; this standard unit conversion is frequently asked in competitive exams.
When a force acts perpendicular to displacement (θ = 90°), such as centripetal force or carrying a load horizontally, the work done is ZERO.
Newton's First Law provides the definition of force, while Newton's Second Law gives the quantitative measurement of force (F = ma).

blocks.content: Formula: Power = Work / Time
SI Unit of Power = Watt (W)
Important Facts
• SI unit of force is Newton.
• Work is measured in Joule.
• F = ma represents Newton’s Second Law of Motion.
• Power is the rate of doing work.
